consumers.preflight: Installer service preflight before install or repair (tools/msi-check)
consumers.system-reload: System manager unit load and daemon-reload of units
consumers.system-enable: System manager enable and disable records under enabled\<target>
consumers.journal-store: System manager unit journal files under journal
consumers.linger-store: Linger grant records under linger, read at startup and by enable-linger
consumers.admission-probe: Delegated admission probe, SYSTEM impersonating the user, over the user's units directory
consumers.os-acl: Windows access checks on the caller's own operation; no product code runs

unsafe-directories.statement: The data root and its immediate units, enabled, journal, runtime, linger and daemon directories conflict when they are a reparse point, not owned by SYSTEM or Administrators, or writable by another principal; new directories inherit the data-root ACL, which grants control to SYSTEM and Administrators only.

no-recursive-follow.statement: Inspect existing privileged directories, reject unexpected reparse points and do not recursively follow links to repair ACLs.

enable-records.statement: Enable writes small files under <base-dir>\enabled\<target>\<unit>, not NTFS symlinks.

delegation-regular-files.statement: A qualifying entry is a regular file with a recognized unit filename in the user's unit directory; untrusted reparse points are not followed to grant admission.

delegation-probe.statement: The probe impersonates the user, pins directory ancestors against replacement and rejects reparse points; delegation rejects UNC and reparse-point paths.

qualified: Junction at the data root, and at the immediate units and linger children, refused by install and repair (Case C and preflight-reparse).
Untrusted owner, non-administrator write grant and custom base directory refused by install and repair (Case C).
Create, write, append, same-parent rename and delete on sentinels inside the protected trees denied to standard and filtered callers (Case C).
Junction in the delegated known-folder path rejected by the admission probe (interactive profile redirection).
Daemon log symlink or reparse chain refused (daemon-log regression).
deferred: Ancestors of a user's profile and %LOCALAPPDATA% above the delegated winunitd directory.
Unsafe or custom parents of the data root or install root, beyond the operating system's default construction.
Reparse races: allowed ancestor or descendant transitions during privileged reads, launches and preflight (R4-P2).
Native producers: the SYSTEM observer of object states, the actor and consumer probes, and the fixture that makes each shape.

cases.title: Junction at enabled\<target> presented to install and repair
cases.question: Must install and repair refuse a reparse point below an immediate data-root child, as they refuse one at the child itself, or is such a pre-existing link supported?
cases.basis: Preflight inspects the data root and its immediate children only; code reading, not observed natively.
cases.recommendation: Characterize install and repair first and keep this undecided until the maintainer chooses the supported policy; a correctly protected root does not by itself establish an unprivileged injection.

cases.title: Enable and disable through a junction at enabled\<target>
cases.question: Must the system manager refuse to read, create or write enable records through a reparse point at enabled\<target>, instead of writing into its target?
cases.basis: Enumeration skips name-surrogate reparse entries, which Go reports as non-directories; enable creates enabled\<target>\<unit> with MkdirAll and WriteFile, which follow an existing junction. Code reading, not observed natively.
cases.recommendation: Characterize the enable and startup consumers first; if links here are unsupported, specify refusal or no-follow per operation and qualify that implementation separately.

cases.title: Junction below units holding a canary unit
cases.question: Are system unit files only the regular files directly in units, so that nested directories and links below it are ignored, as the loader does today?
cases.basis: The loader reads only the top-level entries of units and skips directories and entries without a unit name; code reading, not observed natively.
cases.recommendation: Document top-level regular unit files as the supported loading scope, so nested contents stay ignored as the loader does today; direct unit-file symbolic links need their own explicit policy.

cases.title: File symbolic link in units naming a unit outside
cases.question: Is a unit file in units that is a symbolic link to a file outside the data root supported configuration, refused, or ignored?
cases.recommendation: Give direct unit-file symbolic links their own explicit policy rather than inferring it from the nested-directory case.
cases.basis: The loader opens a top-level entry with a unit name through an ordinary open, which follows a symbolic link; code reading, not observed natively.

cases.title: File link in journal at a unit's journal file
cases.question: Must the journal store refuse a reparse point at a unit's journal file, as the daemon log does, instead of appending through it?
cases.basis: The journal store opens a unit's journal file for create and append with an ordinary open, which follows a link; the daemon log alone opens with reparse-point refusal. Code reading, not observed natively.
cases.recommendation: Characterize the journal store first and keep this undecided until the maintainer chooses the supported policy.

cases.title: File link at a linger record
cases.question: Must the linger store refuse a reparse point at a grant record when it reads it, instead of reading the link's target as the grant?
cases.basis: The linger store reads a record with an ordinary open, which follows a link, and writes one by renaming a new file over the record, which replaces the link itself. Code reading, not observed natively.
cases.recommendation: Characterize the linger store first and keep this undecided until the maintainer chooses the supported policy.

cases.title: Junction below the user's units holding the only unit
cases.basis: The probe reports whether a regular file with a unit name exists directly in units and skips directory and reparse entries; it does not read file contents, so the witness is its admission result: not admitted with only the unit behind the junction, admitted for the peer's regular unit.

cases.title: Symbolic link in the user's units naming a unit outside
cases.basis: The probe skips entries with the reparse-point attribute while it looks for a unit file; with only the linked unit present it must not admit the account.

cases.title: Junction at the user's winunitd directory above units
cases.diagnostic: unit directory contains a reparse point or non-directory
cases.basis: The probe opens every path component with reparse-point semantics and refuses a reparse point; the qualified redirection case put the junction at the known folder, not here.

cases.title: Standard caller renames an immediate data-root child
cases.basis: The data root grants control to SYSTEM and Administrators only, so a caller has no delete or delete-child right on its children.

cases.title: Filtered administrator renames an immediate data-root child
cases.basis: The data root grants control to SYSTEM and Administrators only; a filtered token holds Administrators for deny only.

cases.title: Standard caller with %ProgramData% rights renames the data root
cases.question: Is the operating system's default %ProgramData% ACL the supported ancestor policy for the data root, so that preflight need not inspect ancestors, and must a caller who can create folders there still be denied renaming or replacing the data root?
cases.basis: Preflight inspects the data root and its children but not %ProgramData%. Ordinary callers can create folders there by default, which the control demonstrates; that right is not the right to remove or rename another child, so the actor's effective delete-child right on %ProgramData% and delete right on the data root are measured. Not observed natively.
cases.recommendation: Retain the supported default protected construction; measure effective mutation rights on the actual parent and document unsafe or custom parents as limits. A folder-create right alone does not justify a delete-child threat claim.

cases.title: Filtered administrator with %ProgramData% rights renames the data root
cases.question: Is the operating system's default %ProgramData% ACL the supported ancestor policy for the data root, so that preflight need not inspect ancestors, and must a caller who can create folders there still be denied renaming or replacing the data root?
cases.basis: Preflight inspects the data root and its children but not %ProgramData%. Ordinary callers can create folders there by default, which the control demonstrates; that right is not the right to remove or rename another child, so the actor's effective delete-child right on %ProgramData% and delete right on the data root are measured. Not observed natively.
cases.recommendation: Retain the supported default protected construction; measure effective mutation rights on the actual parent and document unsafe or custom parents as limits. A folder-create right alone does not justify a delete-child threat claim.

cases.title: Standard caller renames the install root through %ProgramFiles%
cases.question: Is the operating system's default %ProgramFiles% ACL the supported ancestor policy for the install root, which preflight inspects but whose parent it does not, so that a caller must be denied renaming or replacing the install root?
cases.recommendation: Retain the supported default protected construction; measure the actor's effective rights on %ProgramFiles% and the install root, and document unsafe or custom parents as limits.
cases.basis: Preflight inspects the install root and bin but not %ProgramFiles%; renaming the install root needs delete on it or delete-child on %ProgramFiles%, which are measured. Not observed natively.

cases.question: Is the operating system's default %ProgramFiles% ACL the supported ancestor policy for the install root, which preflight inspects but whose parent it does not, so that a caller must be denied renaming or replacing the install root?
cases.recommendation: Retain the supported default protected construction; measure the actor's effective rights on %ProgramFiles% and the install root, and document unsafe or custom parents as limits.
